en_summary: Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas in new @SpaceX note: Getting others to pay for compute infrastructure that SpaceX will use to train its robots is a good idea, seeing neocloud build as a funding strategy exploiting advantages in intelligence-per-watt-per-$-per-second. Agrees with Elon that Physical Intelligence Economy is economically multiplicative. Believes $SPCX’s ability to improve the PR image of the AI/SI trade is under-appreciated. SpaceX is undergoing a metamorphosis into a vertically-integrated full-stack AI player, undetected by a market that still views it as a neocloud with exo-atmospheric chops.
ko_summary: 모건스탠리의 Adam Jonas가 새로운 @SpaceX 노트에서 밝혔습니다. 다른 사람들이 SpaceX가 궁극적으로 자체 로봇 훈련에 사용할 컴퓨팅 인프라에 비용을 지불하게 하는 것은 좋은 아이디어이며, 네오클라우드 구축을 자금 조달 전략으로 보고 지능-와트-달러-초당 비교 우위를 활용합니다. Elon의 물리적 지능 경제가 경제적으로 곱셈 효과가 있다는 데 동의합니다. $SPCX가 AI/SI 거래의 PR 이미지를 개선하는 능력이 과소평가되고 있다고 믿습니다. SpaceX는 시장이 여전히 외기권 능력을 가진 네오클라우드로 보는 것을 넘어 수직 통합된 풀스택 AI 플레이어로 변모하고 있습니다.
text:
Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas in new @SpaceX note:

“Getting other people to pay for your own compute infrastructure that you will ultimately use to train your own robots is a good idea. We see the neocloud build as more of a 'funding strategy' where SpaceX can exploit its comparative advantages in maximizing  intelligence-per-watt-per-$-per-second relative to peers.

We agree with Elon that the Physical Intelligence Economy (PIE) is economically multiplicative - if not by an order of mag. We believe $SPCX’s ability to help improve the rather challenging PR image of the AI/SI
trade is quite under-appreciated today.

SpaceX is undergoing a metamorphosis largely undetected by a stock market that still views the company as a neocloud with exo-atsmospheric chops, and not a vertically-integrated, full-stack AI player.”

I have been psychologically short $NFLX for years and believe this year has vindicated that psychological short.

Unfortunately I was way too much of a chicken to actually short/buy puts 😂

In all seriousness, my bear case has always been that they cannot keep up content spend to justify their growth without massive hits. The massive hits have faded away which has significantly hurt the type of subscriber/adgrowth needed for the stock to expand from its premium multiple. 

YouTube’s algorithm was another bear case. How does Netflix compete with a creator economy that is growing rapidly without spending even more money? The move to buy Warner Bros, live sports, podcasting…all of it was to hide that they just don’t have the massive hits needed to keep growing. 

HOWEVER…at some point, the company becomes too cheap. Valuation is 5 year low and they are buying back a ton of stock. I genuinely don’t see how they get back to massive growth again without a MAJOR hit like Squid Games…all the ads/NFL/videogames/buybacks in the world won’t get the street excited without hits.

But I wonder if the margin of safety has finally gotten to the point where their most is being meaningfully discounted (I do think they have a large moat with huge barriers to entry) and if the stock price is officially reflecting that.

Are you buying the dip?

en_summary: AI-related borrowing is skyrocketing. US Dollar-denominated AI-related corporate bond issuance up to $419 billion so far in 2026, highest annual figure on record. +90% YoY from full-year 2025 and +437% from full-year 2024. Year-to-date, Alphabet, $GOOG and others.
ko_summary: AI 관련 차입이 급증하고 있다. 2026년 현재까지 달러 표시 AI 관련 기업 채권 발행이 4190억 달러로, 연간 최고 기록. 2025년 전체 대비 +90% YoY, 2024년 전체 대비 +437% 증가. 연초 현재 Alphabet, $GOOG 등.
text:
AI-related borrowing is skyrocketing.

US Dollar-denominated AI-related corporate bond issuance is up to $419 billion so far in 2026, the highest annual figure on record.

This represents a +90% YoY increase from full-year 2025 and a +437% increase from full-year 2024.

Year-to-date, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, and Oracle, $ORCL, have issued a combined $157 billion in corporate bonds, accounting for 37% of the total.

This is followed by investment-grade and high-yield data center and computing companies, which have raised $66 billion and $37 billion, respectively, and together account for ~25% of AI-related issuance.

Other AI-linked corporate bonds have represented $159 billion, or 38%.

The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.

name: Shay Boloor
